title: Hotel Master
intro: The Hotel Master is the list of hotels: each hotel's code (HTL-…), name, location, contacts, room types and status. A new hotel is added under **Master Files → Supplier**. Everything else is on **Hotel Rates (new)** → the hotel → **Hotel details**, **Room types** and **History**. Prices are in the **Hotel Rates** manual.

guide.title: Step by step
guide.intro: From a new hotel to a tidy hotel list. The numbers in the pictures match the numbers in the text.

stages.title: Stage 1 — Add a new hotel
stages.who: Whoever keeps the suppliers (the Supplier permission)

steps.title: Open New Supplier
steps.text: Open **Master Files → Supplier**. The **New Supplier** form opens.

steps.title: Choose Hotel
steps.text: In **Supplier Catogory** (1) choose **Hotel**. **Hotel Code** (2) fills in by itself with the next number — nobody types it.

steps.title: Type the hotel
steps.text: Type the **Supplier Name** (3) exactly as the hotel calls itself, and the **Location** (4). If you have them, add the reservations **Email** and **Tel No (Home)** (5): they become the hotel's **Reservations e-mail** and **Reservations phone** on the Hotel Master.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Click **Save** (6). The message reads *Supplier Added successfully! Hotel code HTL-… — the hotel is on the Hotel Master.* The hotel is now on **Hotel Rates (new)** with the label **Incomplete — Rates Pending** until its rates are entered and approved (see the **Hotel Rates** manual).

stages.title: Stage 2 — Find and open a hotel

steps.title: Search the hotel list
steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** (on the Tour Desk bar: **Masters → Hotel Rates**). Type a name, town, chain or hotel code in **Search hotel, location, chain or code…** (1). The buttons under it (2) narrow the list: **Frequently Used Hotels**, **No rate today**, **Has drafts**, **Used last year**, **Ends in … days**. The ☆ (3) marks a hotel Frequently Used. The label on the right (4) says whether the hotel has a rate today. The line at the bottom (5) counts the hotels.

steps.title: Open the hotel
steps.text: Click the hotel. Its head shows the **hotel code** (1), **Frequently Used** (2), and the location, supplier account, status, currency and taxes (3). **···** (4) is Management's menu. The tabs (5) hold the rest: **Room types**, **Hotel details** and **History** are the Hotel Master; the rate tabs are in the **Hotel Rates** manual.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Keep the hotel's details right

steps.title: Hotel details
steps.text: Click **Hotel details** (1). The **Hotel code** (2) never changes. Correct the name, location, chain, star category, address, website, **Reservations e-mail** and **Reservations phone** (3), sales contact, accounts e-mail, check-in and check-out times, currency, **Taxes in rates**, tax note, bank details and notes. **Status** (4) is changed by Management only. Click **Save hotel** (5); the message reads *Hotel updated.*

steps.title: Room types
steps.text: Click **Room types** (1). To add a room, type it in **Add a room type** (2) exactly as the hotel writes it and click **Add**. To correct a room, change its **Name** (3) or **Priced as** (4), scroll the table to the right and click **Save** on that row. A room the hotel no longer sells: set its **Status** to *inactive* — rooms are not deleted.

steps.title: History
steps.text: Click **History** (1): every change to the hotel record, with **When**, **Who** and **What** (2). A hotel nobody has changed shows *No changes recorded yet.*

stages.title: Stage 4 — Keep the list tidy
stages.who: Hotel Rate Approval (merging) · Management, Tour Desk Admin (archiving)

steps.title: The same hotel twice
steps.text: Click **Duplicates** on the toolbar. **Possible duplicate hotels** (1) lists hotels that may be on file twice. Someone with **Hotel Rate Approval** clicks **Keep this one** (2) on the record to keep and confirms: the other record's plans, room types and supplier code move across. When the two are in different towns they are usually two hotels of one brand — the system then asks you to type MERGE. A merge can be undone: open the kept hotel and click **Undo merge**.

steps.title: Archive or restore a hotel
steps.text: Management clicks **···** (1). The menu (2) shows first what depends on the hotel, then **Archive (set inactive)…** (or **Restore (set active)** for an archived hotel). Archiving takes the hotel out of the inquiry pickers. Its rates and the nights on file keep their figures; nothing is deleted.

topics.needs_note: Adding a hotel needs the **Supplier** permission (Master Files → Supplier).
topics.summary: A hotel is added once, as a supplier: **Master Files → Supplier**, **Supplier Catogory** *Hotel*, then **Save**. The system gives it its hotel code and puts it on the Hotel Master by itself.

steps.text: Open **Master Files → Supplier**. The **New Supplier** form opens.
In **Supplier Catogory** choose **Hotel**. **Hotel Code** fills in by itself.
Type the **Supplier Name** exactly as the hotel calls itself, and the **Location**. Add the reservations **Email** and **Tel No (Home)** if you have them.
Click **Save**. The message reads *Supplier Added successfully! Hotel code HTL-… — the hotel is on the Hotel Master.*
Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and search the hotel: it shows with **Incomplete — Rates Pending** until its rates are entered and approved.

notes: If the message says *Please choose a different supplier name.*, the hotel is already a supplier: search it on **Hotel Rates (new)** instead of adding it again.
Do not add a hotel a second time under a slightly different name. If it happened, see *The same hotel is on the list twice*.

topics.title: What the labels in the hotel list mean
questions: What does Incomplete — Rates Pending mean?
What do the labels next to the hotels mean?
What does rate today mean?
What does gap today mean?
topics.needs_note: The hotel list needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission.
topics.summary: The label on the right of each hotel says whether a quotation can price it today, from the **approved** published plans.

steps.text: **rate today** (green): an approved plan prices today.

**Incomplete — Rates Pending** (red): the hotel has no approved published contract rate yet. It is on the master for identification and preparation; it gives no quotation price until its rates are entered and approved.

**no rate** (red): nothing approved at all. **expired …** (amber): the last approved plan ended on that date. **from …** (amber): the next plan starts on that date. **gap today** (amber): plans exist, but none covers today.
**draft** (blue): a plan is waiting for approval. **inactive** (grey): the hotel is archived.

notes: To fix a red or amber label, the hotel's rates are entered and approved — see the **Hotel Rates** manual (*Upload a hotel rate sheet*, *Approve hotel rates*).

has: No valid published contract rate yet

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click the hotel.
Click the **Hotel details** tab.

Correct what is wrong: **Hotel name**, **Location**, **Chain / management company**, **Star category**, **Address**, **Website**, **Reservations e-mail**, **Reservations phone**, **Sales contact**, **Accounts e-mail**, **Check-in time**, **Check-out time**, **Currency**, **Taxes in rates**, **Tax note**, **Bank details**, **Notes**.
Click **Save hotel**. The message reads *Hotel updated.*

topics.title: The hotel's reservations e-mail (booking letters)
questions: How do I change a hotel's reservations e-mail?
Where does the booking letter get the hotel's e-mail address?
The booking e-mail goes to the wrong address
How do I add the hotel's e-mail address?
topics.needs_note: Changing it on the Hotel Master needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission.
topics.summary: A hotel's booking letters go to the **Reservations e-mail** on its **Hotel details**. Change it there once and every new letter uses it.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click the hotel.
Click **Hotel details**, correct **Reservations e-mail** (and **Reservations phone**), click **Save hotel**.

On **Hotel Bookings**, a hotel with no reservations e-mail shows an empty **To** box: type the address and tick **Also save this address on the Hotel Master as the hotel's Reservations e-mail (for every future booking)**.

notes: An address typed on one booking without the tick is kept for that stay only; the Hotel Master is not changed.

topics.title: The hotel code (HTL-…)
questions: What is the hotel code?
How do I give a hotel its code?
Can I change a hotel code?
What is the difference between H and HTL codes?
topics.summary: Every hotel has a permanent code **HTL-…**, given by the system when the hotel is created. Nobody types or changes it; it stays when the hotel is renamed or archived.

steps.text: A new hotel gets its code when it is saved under **Master Files → Supplier** (**Hotel Code** fills in by itself).
The supplier's **H**-number and the Hotel Master's **HTL**-number are the same number: H336 is HTL-336.
Search by code on **Hotel Rates (new)**: *HTL-017*, *htl17* or *17* all find the hotel.

has: Hotel code — permanent, given by the system; it stays if the hotel is renamed or archived
permanent — given by the system, kept through renames and archiving

topics.needs_note: Editing room types needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission.
topics.summary: Open the hotel → **Room types** tab. Add a room with **Add a room type**. Keep one name per room.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click the hotel.
Open the **Room types** tab.
To add a room: type its name in **Add a room type** exactly as the hotel writes it, click **Add**.
**Priced as**: *base rate* when the sheet prints its own prices, *base + suppl.* when it is another room plus a supplement. Scroll the table to the right and click **Save** on the row.
Two names for the same room, or a room no longer sold: use one name in every plan and set the other row's **Status** to *inactive*. Rooms are not deleted.

topics.title: The same hotel is on the list twice
questions: The same hotel is on the list twice
How do I merge two hotels?
A hotel was created twice with different names
How do I undo a merge?
topics.needs_note: Anyone with **Hotel Rates (new)** can see **Duplicates**; merging needs **Hotel Rate Approval**.
topics.summary: **Duplicates** on the Hotel Rates toolbar lists hotels that may be on file twice. Someone with **Hotel Rate Approval** keeps one record and folds the other into it. A merge can be undone.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click **Duplicates** on the toolbar.
**Possible duplicate hotels** lists each group with its town, supplier account, plans and tour nights. Check it is really the same hotel.

Click **Keep this one** on the record to keep and confirm. The other record's plans, room types and supplier code move across; it is hidden from the quotation lists; its ledger history is not touched.
When the hotels are in **different locations** they are usually two hotels of one brand. Merge only if you are sure — the system asks you to type MERGE.
To undo: open the kept hotel and click **Undo merge** beside the hotel it absorbed.

notes: Two copies of the same *rate sheet* (not the same hotel) are a different thing: see *Same sheet uploaded twice* in the **Hotel Rates** manual.

topics.title: Archive or restore a hotel (take it out of use)
questions: How do I deactivate a hotel?
How do I archive a hotel we no longer use?
How do I delete a hotel?
How do I restore an archived hotel?
topics.needs_note: Archiving and restoring a hotel needs **Tour Desk Admin** (Management). The **···** button shows only for them.
topics.summary: Hotels are not deleted. Management archives a hotel (sets it inactive) from **···** on the hotel's page: it leaves the inquiry pickers, and its rates and nights on file stay. It can be restored.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click the hotel.
Click **···** (Manage). The menu first shows **Depends on it**: approved plans, drafts, nights on open inquiries, open cards on the Hotel Desk and tour nights in the last year.
Click **Archive (set inactive)…**, write why if you like, click **Archive**.
To bring it back: **···** → **Restore (set active)**.

notes: Archiving is refused while stays at this hotel are open on the Hotel Desk: finish or archive those cards first.
Archived hotels stay in the list with the label **inactive**.

topics.title: Who can add or change hotels?
questions: Who can add a new hotel?
Who can change hotel details?
Why can I not see the ··· button?
Who can merge or archive hotels?
topics.summary: Each action follows a menu permission given to your user group.

steps.text: Add a hotel: **Supplier** (Master Files → Supplier).
See hotels, change **Hotel details**, **Room types**, **Frequently Used**: **Hotel Rates (new)**.
Merge duplicate hotels: **Hotel Rate Approval**.
Archive or restore a hotel (the **···** button): **Tour Desk Admin** (Management).
Missing one? Ask your manager; the System Administrator gives it under **Settings → Group Privileges**.
